newsitem.title: UK: Enterprise hits record after Italy news.
newsitem.headline: Enterprise hits record after Italy news.

text.p: Shares in Enterprise Oil Plc hit a record high in early trading on Thursday amid renewed demand following Wednesday's upbeat news on the company's drilling operations in southern Italy, dealers and analysts said.
Recent analyst briefings by the company's chief executive Pier Jungels could also be boosting interest in the stock, they added.
The stock was up 26p at 680 by 0908 GMT after earlier touching a record 684p -- up some 60p or 9.6 percent on the week. Trading volume reached 1.1 million shares.

On Wednesday Simon Oddie, Enterprise general manager in Rome, said results from an appraisal of the Cerro Falcone discovery in the south Appenine area had been "excellent" and the field would be go into long-term production later this year.
"The Italian discovery is growing and growing" said Tony Alves, analyst at Henderson Crosthwaite. "We are seeing further positive impact from yesterday's story."
Steve Turner, analyst at HSBC James Capel, agreed.
"I think it is follow-through from yesterday's very good announcement from Italy," Turner said. "I didn't think the market yesterday fully appreciated how good the news was."
The drilling report meant more reserves, more production and lower costs for Enterprise's Italian operations, he said.

Alves said recent analyst meetings with Jungels had reinforced positive views towards Enterprise, along with further strength in crude prices against a backdrop of colder-than-usual U.S. weather forecasts and signs of a power struggle in Iraq.
Earlier this week Enterprise shares gained after the group confirmed a crude oil discovery in the Gulf of Mexico, the first result of an exploration partnership with Pennzoil.
